subject: Intermittent p95 tail spikes — proposed mitigation and carveout request
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heronfin.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, contracts@heronfin.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent high p95 latency affecting transaction flow

Hi Aisha —

We're seeing intermittent p95 tail spikes across a subset of our production traffic this morning starting ~08:40 PDT. Symptoms:
- p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~180ms -> 1.9s for ~7% of requests (5m windows)
- error rate remains low (<0.5%) but user-facing latency causes renewals flow timeouts
- spike correlates with higher sequence lengths (>=600 tokens) and a rollout timestamp at 07:45

Attached are logs and a small sample trace set (heronfin_latency_logs_20270516.zip). Can your team investigate and tell us whether you can fallback the model variant or apply a temporary routing/carveout? We need a mitigation plan within the hour if possible — this is impacting our SSO-based onboarding flows.

If a rollback is required, we need to understand risk: will a rollback increase token usage or change outputs significantly for edge cases? Also looping in contracts in case we need a short-term SLA amendment.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
CTO | HeronFin
liam.oconnor@heronfin.com
[attachment: heronfin_latency_logs_20270516.zip (application/zip)]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heronfin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high p95 latency affecting transaction flow

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick heads-up and for sending the logs. We're prioritizing this. I want to loop in Marissa (runtime), Karthik (SRE), and Tessa (CS/partnership) so we can put an action plan on the table.

Proposed immediate next steps (will confirm in 10m):
- Engineering: triage logs and determine whether the 07:45 rollout corresponds to a model variant (v7.3) or a kernel/config change
- If a variant change is the root cause, propose a controlled rollback to v7.2 in us-west-2 as a canary (target 60% of HeronFin traffic)
- If rollback is not safe, propose an automated prefix/KV cache warmup and temporary traffic pin to lower-latency variant while we fix the regression
- Request: can HeronFin sign a short emergency SLA carveout (48h) to allow fallback and traffic changes while we remediate? I attached a draft proposal (SLA_carveout_proposal_v1.pdf) for your legal team.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm the ETA for a root-cause determination and whether controlled rollback is feasible with minimal output drift?

Liam — please confirm if we have permission to start a canary rollback in 20–30 minutes pending your approval.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com]
[attachment: SLA_carveout_proposal_v1.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@heronfin.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high p95 latency affecting transaction flow

Quick triage notes (from runtime traces and kernels):
- Rollout Id matches model:v7.3-deploy at 07:44:52 PDT — confirmed by rollout metadata
- Observed pattern: KV cache miss amplification when sequence length > 500 combined with a change in attention kernel selection in v7.3 that is not yet fully warmed for certain GPU tiling paths
- p95 increase matches the timeline and is concentrated on requests hitting tokenized long-context paths (onboarding flows as reported)

Mitigation options and risks:
1) Canary rollback to v7.2 (recommended):
   - Plan: deploy v7.2 variant as a canary in us-west-2 at 60% of HeronFin traffic for 30 minutes, monitor p95 and correctness on canary sample
   - Risk: small subset of long-context generations may show slight semantic differences; overall token usage unchanged
   - Rollback time estimate: ~12–18 minutes to shift with safe rollback hooks

2) Prefix/KV warmup + kernel patch (longer):
   - Warmup could reduce p95 but will take hours to fully stabilize across all nodes

Recommendation: option (1) now for immediate p95 mitigation, then follow-up (2) as a post-mortem fix.

I've attached a short runtime snippet for the team to look at (runtime_snippet.txt). Aisha — we need customer approval to proceed with canary.

— Marissa
VP, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

- Need documented approval for a temporary SLA carveout to avoid automatic SLO breach billing triggers while we act — recommend 48h carveout window.
- I'll prepare the runbook and page the on-call to be on standby; ETA for canary ops start: 20m after customer permission.

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan and authorization request — canary rollback + temporary carveout

Hi Liam and HeronFin legal —

Thanks for your patience. Based on engineering triage we propose the following immediate plan:

1) Authorization requested — Canary rollback to model v7.2 in us-west-2
   - Traffic: start at ~60% HeronFin traffic (can be limited by route)
   - Timing: begin canary within 20 minutes of your approval; monitoring window 30 minutes
   - Success criteria: p95 returns to baseline (<= 240ms) for two consecutive 5m windows and no increase in error rate

2) Contingency 
   - If p95 does not improve, we'll execute a full rollback for us-west-2 and open an incident bridge for immediate follow-up

3) Temporary SLA carveout request (48 hours)
   - Purpose: avoid automatic SLO enforcement and to give engineering the ability to change routing/variants without triggering billing/penalties while we remediate
   - We've attached a short amendment draft for legal to review (SLA_carveout_proposal_v1.pdf). If acceptable we can DocuSign an emergency amendment now: https://docusign.example/emergency-amendment/DF-4391

Please reply with an explicit approval line (e.g., "HeronFin approves canary rollback + 48h carveout") if you want us to proceed. If we don't hear back within 20 minutes we'll hold off executing.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here. We'll operate transparently and share metrics live in the incident doc: https://app.redwoodinference.com/ops/incidents/DF-4391

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
